newsitem.title: INDIA: India Congress chides Gujral government.
newsitem.headline: India Congress chides Gujral government.

text.p: India's Congress party warned Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Saturday that while it would continue to give his minority coalition vital support it was unhappy with government performance.
The Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP), an apex panel of the party's deputies, met in the Indian capital to discuss the prevailing political situation.
"Some concerns on the functioning of the United Front government were voiced at the CPP meeting," a Congress leader, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
The Press Trust of India said Congress president Sitaram Kesri gave indications of his party's displeasure over the government's functioning.

Congress criticised Gujral's government for its record in a wide range of issues, from rising violence and separatist insurgencies to inter-state relations and the government's failure to tackle a burgeoning oil subsidy bill, PTI said.
Congress will take up various issues for discussion with the United Front (UF) leadership, party sources said.
"Our position is clear we will continue to support the government," Congress spokesman V.N. Gadgil told Reuters.

Congress which has ruled India for all but five years since independence from Britain in 1947, suffered its worst electoral defeat last year, but still wields clout through its make-or-break support for the ruling coalition.

Kesri plunged the United Front into a crisis in March by withdrawing his party's support, leading to the defeat of prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition in a parliamentary confidence vote on April 11.
The UF then chose Gujral as the new prime minister to win back Congress support.
The pledge of continued support will be some relief to Gujral, who faces mounting pressure from some of his alliance partners to ditch his former party chief.
The popular chief minister of eastern state of Bihar Laloo Prasad Yadav broke away from the Gujral's Janata Dal party last week and formed a rebel group called Rashtriya (Nationalist) Janata Dal.
Yadav, who was the president of Janata Dal before the split, has been indicted in a $280 million corruption scandal but says he is innocent.
Yadav has decided to face a confidence vote in the Bihar assembly during the monsoon session, which begins on Monday.
Gujral's left wing allies have urged him to recommend Yadav's dismissal as state chief.
Yadav may seek Congress support to win the confidence vote in the state legislature and thwart moves to dislodge him.
